data.title: ScienceDaily: That fresh cleaning smell could be filling your home with nanoparticles
data.summary: Researchers found that scented cleaners can react with ozone indoors to create billions or trillions of invisible nanoparticles that can penetrate deep into the lungs. The pollution forms within minutes and, in some cases, may produce an inhaled particle dose comparable to or greater than standing near heavy traffic.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: That fresh cleaning smell could be filling your home with nanoparticles

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth
data.summary: Scientists have found that a famous 2-billion-year-old chemical signature, once thought to record a massive global change in Earth’s carbon cycle, may instead have been produced by local magma, hydrocarbons, and methane-eating microbes. The discovery raises new questions about what was really happening as oxygen transformed the young planet.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists burned their own scrolls to unlock a 2,000-year-old mystery
data.summary: Scientists discovered that tiny amounts of lead in ancient ink can make writing inside burned papyrus scrolls stand out dramatically in X-ray scans. The technique could help unlock lost Greek and Roman texts preserved by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius nearly 2,000 years ago.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists burned their own scrolls to unlock a 2,000-year-old mystery

data.title: ScienceDaily: Quantum computer simulates matter “popping into existence”
data.summary: Scientists recreated a particle-forming process linked to the extreme physics of the early universe using a 13-ion quantum simulator. The breakthrough suggests quantum computers could eventually help researchers investigate how matter formed and evolved after the Big Bang.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Quantum computer simulates matter “popping into existence”

data.title: ScienceDaily: Two astronauts who flew farther than anyone before are taking new NASA roles
data.summary: Artemis II astronauts Victor Glover and Reid Wiseman are transitioning to emeritus status at NASA after their historic journey around the Moon earlier this year. The pair will continue advising and mentoring NASA teams as preparations accelerate for Artemis III and future lunar missions. Their experience with Orion and deep-space operations could prove especially valuable as NASA works toward returning astronauts to the lunar surface.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Two astronauts who flew farther than anyone before are taking new NASA roles

data.title: ScienceDaily: Zepbound and Mounjaro may turn on the body’s calorie-burning brown fat
data.summary: Tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, activated calorie-burning brown fat in obese mice, revealing a potential metabolic effect beyond appetite suppression. If confirmed in humans, the finding could help explain the drug’s powerful benefits and inspire more comprehensive treatments for obesity and diabetes.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Zepbound and Mounjaro may turn on the body’s calorie-burning brown fat

data.title: ScienceDaily: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
data.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops. The finding suggests that dreaming may require such intense internal processing that neurons consume energy faster than it can be replenished.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discovered two bizarre new sea spiders that are “nightmare fuel”
data.summary: Scientists discovered two strange new sea spider species in the Salish Sea, including a hairy-legged, red-eyed species that can groom itself with comb-like appendages. Another is frequently covered in tiny parasites, and researchers say many more undiscovered sea spiders may still be hiding in the region.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists discovered two bizarre new sea spiders that are “nightmare fuel”

data.title: ScienceDaily: CERN has begun disconnecting the Large Hadron Collider
data.summary: CERN has started replacing some of the Large Hadron Collider’s most important magnets as part of its High-Luminosity upgrade. The new superconducting magnets will produce fields about 40% stronger, allowing particle beams to be squeezed more tightly before they collide. That should create far more collisions for the ATLAS and CMS experiments to analyze, giving physicists a much larger window into the fundamental workings of the universe.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: CERN has begun disconnecting the Large Hadron Collider

data.title: ScienceDaily: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
data.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia. Lab experiments suggest the popular joint supplement may intensify an abnormal sugar-tagging process in the Alzheimer’s brain, although researchers say clinical trials are needed to determine whether it actually causes harm.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression

data.title: ScienceDaily: Atrial fibrillation patients saw 69% lower risk with common blood thinners
data.summary: Direct oral anticoagulants cut the risk of serious clinical events by 69% in atrial fibrillation patients with an intermediate risk of stroke, according to the randomized SINGLE-AF trial. The benefit was driven mainly by fewer ischemic strokes, with no increase in major bleeding.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Atrial fibrillation patients saw 69% lower risk with common blood thinners

data.title: ScienceDaily: One CRISPR treatment cut “bad” cholesterol in half for a full year
data.summary: A single dose of an experimental CRISPR therapy cut LDL cholesterol and triglycerides by about half in patients with difficult-to-treat lipid disorders. The reductions were still present one year later, with the highest dose lowering LDL by 52.5% and triglycerides by 47.8%.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: One CRISPR treatment cut “bad” cholesterol in half for a full year

data.title: ScienceDaily: New soil test could reveal how soil microbes help feed plants
data.summary: Scientists have streamlined a method for measuring DNA-bound phosphorus in soil, making it cheaper and easier while preserving its accuracy. The technique could reveal how soil microbes help recycle phosphorus and ultimately support more sustainable fertilizer and nutrient management.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: New soil test could reveal how soil microbes help feed plants

data.title: ScienceDaily: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life
data.summary: Scientists studying ancient Australian rocks uncovered more than 12,000 fossils from some of the oldest known eukaryotes on Earth. These early complex cells lived in settings ranging from coastal mudflats to the open sea, but only where oxygen was available. Oxygen-free environments contained simpler microbes instead. The findings strengthen the idea that oxygen played a crucial role in the emergence of complex life.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life

data.title: ScienceDaily: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
data.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms. Researchers say identifying these hidden drivers could prevent unnecessary medication changes and lead to more personalized treatment.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control

data.title: ScienceDaily: These medieval graves looked like family burials. DNA told a different story
data.summary: Ancient DNA shows that adults and children buried together in medieval Sweden were often not members of the same immediate family, suggesting that burial choices reflected more than biological kinship. The research also revealed early gender-based burial customs and uncovered the remarkable story of a young woman who may have completed a pilgrimage across Europe.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: These medieval graves looked like family burials. DNA told a different story

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists say house cats could help unlock better cancer treatments for humans
data.summary: Scientists have mapped the genetics of cat cancer on an unprecedented scale and found surprising similarities with tumors in humans. The findings could help bring precision cancer treatments to cats while also revealing new clues about how human cancers develop and respond to drugs.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists say house cats could help unlock better cancer treatments for humans

data.title: ScienceDaily: Diabetes study finds keeping blood sugar too steady may come at a price
data.summary: People with diabetes reported better quality of life after days when their glucose stayed largely within a healthy range, even when levels fluctuated more than usual. The unexpected finding suggests that pursuing extremely tight glucose control may sometimes come with a hidden lifestyle burden.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Diabetes study finds keeping blood sugar too steady may come at a price

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
data.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain

data.title: ScienceDaily: Blood tests reveal why astronauts get constipated in space
data.summary: Spaceflight may dramatically change the gut within weeks, causing bacteria to break down more protein as food moves more slowly through the intestines. The shift could help explain astronaut constipation and may have wider effects on health, making it an important concern for future missions to Mars.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Blood tests reveal why astronauts get constipated in space

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists were wrong about this strange mammal for nearly 40 years
data.summary: A beautifully preserved fossil from Mongolia’s Gobi Desert has solved a mystery that puzzled paleontologists for nearly 40 years. Tamirkhan balcarceli shows that zhelestids were not early relatives of modern placental mammals, despite having teeth that seemed to suggest they were. Instead, the rabbit-like animal belonged to a separate lineage of small Cretaceous mammals.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists were wrong about this strange mammal for nearly 40 years

data.title: ScienceDaily: James Webb reveals why planet formation is a race against time
data.summary: JWST has revealed that young planetary systems lose their planet-building gas through a changing mix of powerful jets, molecular winds, and radiation-driven outflows. As the disks age and their gas disappears, giant planets face a shrinking window to build massive atmospheres.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: James Webb reveals why planet formation is a race against time

data.title: ScienceDaily: Pomegranate compound improves heart function by up to 80% in study
data.summary: A compound the body can make after eating pomegranates, walnuts, and some berries improved measures of heart function by up to 80% in animal models of a difficult-to-treat form of heart failure. Urolithin A helped stiff heart tissue relax and reduced scarring and abnormal enlargement. It also improved relaxation in engineered human heart tissue.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Pomegranate compound improves heart function by up to 80% in study

data.title: ScienceDaily: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs
data.summary: Scientists resurrected antimicrobial peptides from mammals that lived millions of years ago and found that some were more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than modern human versions. These evolutionary relics could provide new clues for designing treatments as antibiotic resistance becomes an increasingly serious threat.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs

data.title: ScienceDaily: Is the universe infinite? The answer gets weird fast
data.summary: Measurements of ancient light from the cosmic microwave background suggest that the universe is remarkably flat. But that does not prove it is infinite, because the observable cosmos could be only a small patch of a much larger curved universe. Space could even be flat while wrapping around on itself in exotic ways.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Is the universe infinite? The answer gets weird fast

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists found a surprising driver of Alzheimer’s outside the brain
data.summary: Scientists found that immune cells contributing to Alzheimer’s-related brain damage may be activated in lymph nodes outside the brain before traveling into the nervous system. Blocking this pathway in mice dramatically reduced neurodegeneration and preserved cognitive abilities, pointing to a potentially more accessible treatment target.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists found a surprising driver of Alzheimer’s outside the brain

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists expected these Galápagos sea turtles to wander. They stayed put
data.summary: Yellow-morph green sea turtles in the Galápagos surprised scientists by staying remarkably close to home instead of making the long journeys typically associated with sea turtles. data.title: ScienceDaily: Hidden stem cells may be fueling spinal stenosis
data.summary: Scientists have discovered a stem cell that appears to serve as a master source for tendon and ligament cells throughout the body. In lumbar spinal stenosis, these cells become unusually active and may drive the ligament overgrowth that squeezes spinal nerves and causes pain, numbness, and difficulty walking. Researchers found that reducing calcium signaling stopped this abnormal growth in mice.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Hidden stem cells may be fueling spinal stenosis

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists find new virus behind mysterious tick illness

Most patients with ALTNV alone recovered, but coinfections with another dangerous tick-borne virus were linked to more serious complications.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists find new virus behind mysterious tick illness
